To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the brainstem areas that express the NET and TH genes are also the sites of NE synthesis.
the distribution of cells that express NET, NPY, TH and DBH mRNAs is different in the medulla and the pons.
NET, TH and NPY mRNA are expressed by the same or neighboring neurons in the A1, A2, AP, and the LC, LC, LCs and A5 nuclei.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and distribution of NET, NPY, TH and DBH mRNAs in the brainstem.
the identification and localization of NET, NPY, and TH mRNA-expressing cells in the rabbit brain.
the distribution of NET, TH and NPY mRNAs and DBH-positive cells in the rabbit brain stem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rabbit brainstem contains a variety of NE cell populations which are involved in the coital-induced pre-ovulatory surge.
the rabbit medullary A1, A2 and the pontine A5, LC and LCs contain TH and NET mRNAs and NPY cells, while AP expresses TH and NET mRANs but little or no NPy message.
the distribution patterns of TH, NET and NPY mRNA expression in the brainstem of the rabbit were similar to those in other mammals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NET, TH and NPY are expressed in the rabbit brain in a topographically specific manner and are present in the same or adjacent cells in the brainstem.
in the brainstem of the rabbit, the distribution pattern of NET, NPY, TH mRNAs and DBH-positive cells is similar in some regions, but different in others.
the coital signal is transmitted to the medulla and the pons and is integrated into GnRH signals via NE and/or NPY neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in the rabbit, the brainstem areas that express TH, NET and/or the NPY message are the same areas that contain DBH-positive cells.
the distribution of NET, TH and NPY mRNAs is similar in the LC and LCs, A1, A2, A5, and AP in the rabbit.
the expression of NET mRNA appears to be more widespread than TH mRNA in the rabbit brain stem.
